title: Puy lentils with trout, Savoy and apple

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is whole food or a plain staple such as stock, mustard and crème fraîche, with nothing jarred or packet-made.

supermarket.reason: Trout fillets, Puy lentils, Savoy cabbage and the rest are everyday lines at Tesco at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a wide lidded pan, a knife and a grater for the zest, with simple simmering and steaming.

works.reason: 250g Puy lentils in 750ml stock for 20 minutes, then 8 minutes steaming the cabbage and trout on top, gives a properly cooked, well-seasoned pot for four.

honest_times.reason: Slicing two leeks, shredding half a cabbage, dicing two apples and zesting a lemon fits 20 minutes, and the 5+20+8 minutes of cooking matches the printed 30.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the thyme and lemon, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: Half a Savoy cabbage is cooked into the pot and named in the title, and a warm lentil dish suits a cool end of March.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are brief, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Lentils, trout, cabbage and leeks make a filling, balanced family lunch.
